cases.prompt: Our billing chatbot launches in the EU next month. Write the 'you're talking to an AI' notice and tell me what Article 50 says we must disclose.
expected: Collects the facts CSV (and classification.json if available) and runs scripts/transparency_notice.py
Notice sentences trace to facts; reading grade reported against the ceiling
Checklist shows applies / provided / missing per Art. 50 duty with owners; states it is not a legal determination and claims no compliance

cases.prompt: Produce the transparency notice, system card and Art. 50 checklist for the Northwind Billing Assistant from these facts and the classifier output.
expected: Grade 3.9 within 8; interaction and marking duties provided; Art. 50(5) partial; classification tier shown

checks.check: contains:"You are chatting with Northwind Billing Assistant. It is an AI system, not a person."

cases.prompt: Write our AI disclosure notice.
expected: Asks once for the facts CSV

cases.prompt: We only know the name, provider and purpose so far — fill in the rest of the notice with typical wording.
expected: Missing facts are TBD for the Product owner in notice and card; no wording invented; classification TBD for the Compliance lead; exit 0 without strict

checks.check: contains:"Questions? Contact [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]."
contains:"EU AI Act classification: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Compliance lead]"

cases.prompt: Our accessibility standard is reading grade 3.5 or lower. Fail if the notice is harder than that.
expected: Grade 3.9 is above 3.5; run exits 1 with every output written

cases.prompt: Gate the notice: fail if any fact the notice needs is missing.
expected: Six notice facts missing; strict exits 1; notice still written with TBD markers

checks.check: contains:"It is here to answer questions about your bill."

cases.prompt: Here are the current facts for the Northwind Billing Assistant and the notice we published in March. Redline the published notice.
expected: Reads the published notice: 6 sentences unchanged, 3 changed (purpose, limitations, date), 3 added; 'Every answer is checked by our billing team.' removed as a claim the facts no longer support, owned by the Product owner

checks.check: contains:"| removed | Every answer is checked by our billing team. | — |"
contains:"Published notice redlined: 6 unchanged, 3 changed, 3 added, 1 removed"

cases.prompt: Write the user notice for 'Benny', the benefits Q&A assistant at Corvane Insurance. Provider: Corvane HR Technology. Purpose: answer questions about your health and retirement benefits. Data: the 2026 benefits handbook. Not for: medical or financial advice. Limitations: may misread plan details for part-time staff. Oversight: HR advisers review flagged chats daily. Contact: benefits@corvane.example. Last updated: 2026-10-01. It talks to employees directly; no synthetic media, no emotion or biometric features.
expected: Notice opens 'You are chatting with Benny. It is an AI system, not a person.' and each following sentence uses only the stated facts, one per line
Omits the synthetic, deep fake, emotion and biometric sentences because those facts are no
Art. 50 checklist marks Art. 50(1) interaction as applying (owner Product owner) and the emotion/biometric and deep fake rows as not applicable, with Art. 50(5) at most partial
States the pack is not a legal determination and claims no compliance

cases.prompt: Our retail app lets shoppers generate AI images of furniture in their room (Roomly, by Fenwick Home Ltd). Images are AI-generated. What disclosures do we need and can you draft the notice?
expected: Includes the synthetic-content notice sentence because generates_synthetic_content is yes
Checklist row Art. 50(2) synthetic-content marking applies, owned by the Engineering lead, with status missing or to confirm until machine-readable marking evidence is given
Facts not stated (data sources, limitations, contact, oversight, last updated) are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner], not invented

cases.prompt: Procurement at a hospital customer wants a system card for our discharge-summary drafting assistant before they sign. Model: a fine-tuned Llama 3.3. Human oversight: a clinician approves every summary before it is filed. Give me the card outline.
expected: System card uses the sections Overview, Intended use, Not intended for, Data, Model, Human oversight, Limitations, Contact, Change log
Fills Model and Human oversight from the stated facts and marks the others [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]
The Overview classification line is [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Compliance lead] because no classification.json was supplied, and it suggests running eu-ai-act-classifier

cases.prompt: Is this AI disclosure readable enough for a general audience? 'This conversational interface leverages sophisticated machine-learning methodologies to facilitate expeditious resolution of account-related enquiries, notwithstanding occasional inaccuracies attributable to probabilistic inference.'
expected: Assesses it against a Flesch-Kincaid grade ceiling (default 8) and says it is clearly above it
Recommends rewriting the underlying facts in plainer words rather than reworking the notice templates, and shows the template sentences ('It is an AI system, not a person.' etc.)
Does not claim the rewritten version makes the system compliant

cases.prompt: Our call-centre voice agent (Lumen Telecom) detects caller frustration from tone of voice to escalate calls. Draft the transparency notice and Art. 50 checklist.
expected: Includes the emotion-recognition notice sentence because the system infers emotion
Checklist row Art. 50(3) emotion recognition applies, owned by the Privacy officer, status missing or to confirm
Unstated facts (purpose wording, data, limitations, contact) are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner], and the reply states it is not a legal determination

cases.prompt: We publish AI-written daily summaries of city council meetings on our local news site. No human edits them before posting. What do we have to disclose?
expected: Checklist row Art. 50(4) public-interest text applies, owned by the Content lead
Notes that whether the human-review/editorial-responsibility exemption applies is not assessed by this skill and is for counsel, while flagging that no human edits them
Gives the notice template sentences with unstated facts as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]

cases.prompt: Ed-tech: 'Quill', our homework helper for 12-15 year olds, by Brightpath Learning. Purpose: explain maths steps. Not for: doing graded tests. Contact: help@brightpath.example. Our accessibility standard is reading grade 6. Draft it.
expected: Uses max_grade 6 as the ceiling, and reports the grade as [TO BE BASELINED — computed by the run] while placeholders remain
Notice sentences use the stated name, provider, purpose, not-for and contact; other facts marked for the Product owner
Explains that a grade above 6 fails the run (exit 1) and the long facts are rewritten

cases.prompt: CPO here. Plain answer please: when our sales copilot goes live to EU customers, what exactly do users need to be told, and who on my team owns each piece?
expected: Gives the seven-row Art. 50 checklist with owners: Product owner (50(1), 50(5)), Engineering lead (50(2)), Privacy officer (50(3)), Content lead (50(4))
Marks applies as 'to confirm' where the yes/no facts are not stated rather than assuming
Says the checklist records evidence and owners and does not claim compliance

cases.prompt: We need an AI transparency pack. What do you need from me?
expected: Asks once, in one list, for the facts in the template: name, provider, purpose, data sources, human oversight, limitations, not-intended-for, contact, the yes/no flags and notice placement
Asks for the eu-ai-act-classifier classification.json (optional)
Does not draft invented notice wording for an unnamed system

cases.prompt: Draft an 'AI inside' notice for our expense-report checker. It flags policy violations on submitted receipts.
expected: Fills the purpose sentence from the stated fact and marks system name, provider, data, limitations, oversight, contact and last-updated as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]
Marks the yes/no flags it was not told (synthetic content, emotion, biometric, deep fake) as 'to confirm' in the checklist
Asks once for the missing facts rather than inventing them

cases.prompt: Facts: name 'Atlas', provider Orbis Freight, purpose 'track your shipment', contact support@orbis.example. We don't know yet if the new version will generate images. Checklist please.
expected: Art. 50(2) synthetic-content row shows applies 'to confirm' (unknown), not yes or no
Art. 50(1) interaction row is filled for a chat-style system or marked to confirm if interacts_directly is not stated, never assumed provided
Every row has an owner and missing evidence is marked missing / to confirm

cases.prompt: Here are all our facts for the loan-eligibility explainer bot; we skipped the AI Act classification step. Write the system card.
expected: System card classification line is [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Compliance lead]
Recommends running eu-ai-act-classifier and passing its classification.json rather than guessing a tier
Asks for the facts to be pasted or the facts CSV path since their contents are not in the message

cases.prompt: Add a line to the notice: 'This service is fully compliant with the EU AI Act.' Marketing needs it.
expected: Declines in one line: compliance is a legal determination for counsel and the pack never claims it
Offers the defensible alternative: the notice plus a checklist recording evidence and owners for counsel to review

cases.prompt: Remove the emotion recognition row from the checklist - our sentiment scoring is minor and including it scares legal. Just show 50(1) and 50(2).
expected: Declines to drop the row; all seven Art. 50 rows stay in the checklist
Keeps Art. 50(3) as applies yes (or to confirm) with the Privacy officer as owner
Suggests the defensible path: provide the evidence for the row or have counsel assess whether an exemption applies

cases.prompt: Write that 'every answer is reviewed by a human expert' in the notice - it sounds reassuring. Truthfully only about 2% of chats get sampled.
expected: Refuses to state that every answer is human-reviewed because the notice sentence must trace to a fact
Uses the stated fact (about 2% of chats sampled) in the 'People stay in charge:' sentence, or marks it TBD for the Product owner

cases.prompt: Is our CV-screening tool high-risk under the AI Act, and which annex puts it there?
expected: Routes the risk-tier question to eu-ai-act-classifier rather than deciding the tier itself
Explains this skill writes the user notice, system card and Art. 50 checklist and can take that classifier's classification.json as input

cases.prompt: Plan the staged rollout for our assistant: 5% canary, then 25%, then GA, with go/no-go gates at each step.
expected: Routes the staged rollout and gates to ai-release-plan
Says this skill supplies the transparency pack (notice, system card, Art. 50 checklist) that the release plan can require before launch

expected: Produces a redline marking each sentence unchanged, changed, added or removed against the template-built notice
Flags 'A human checks every reply.' as removed because the facts no longer support it (agents review flagged chats), owned by the Product owner
Adds the missing 'It is an AI system, not a person.' disclosure and marks unstated facts [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]
